title: Capacity-matched attention-weighted log-mean-exp control
hypothesis: Replacing the baseline's attention-weighted arithmetic mean of instance logits with an attention-weighted log-mean-exp can give rare high-scoring evidence more influence without hard instance selection or fewer active parameters. With the same encoder, gated attention, classifier, and training protocol, this predicts a smaller paired 16-to-64 discrimination loss under both clean labels and fixed 15% label flips. The prediction fails if gains occur only on 16-patch bags, disappear under label noise, or come with negative-bag probability increases that erase class-margin preservation. The supplied calibration does not establish that dilution occurs in this feature setting; this experiment tests it.
note: Public summary; full source quotations and agent logs are not redistributed.
